transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’m a terrible person and that everything that’s gone wrong is my fault, like I’ve already messed up my whole life. My pastor and my aunt insisted I come talk to someone because I just feel so lost and don't know how to fix any of it.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has it been going on for at least two weeks, or longer?

It's been going on for much longer than two weeks, honestly. It's been a little over a year now, pretty much since I started pushing myself so hard with my GED prep and taking on all those extra shifts. I just haven't been able to shake this darkness since then.
Have you had periods of feeling better for more than a few weeks at a time during this past year, or has your low mood been continuously present?

No, I haven't had any breaks from this that lasted for weeks at all. It's been pretty much constant, and at most, I'll have a rare, brief day where the heavy cloud lifts just a little bit, but then it always comes right back.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies, socializing, or work?

Yes, I really have. Things I used to love, like going to Zumba, weekend hikes, and volunteering at the youth center, just feel completely pointless and far away now. It honestly feels like I'm just watching my life happen from underwater.
Have your feelings of guilt, low mood, and loss of interest been severe enough to significantly impair your ability to function in daily life, such as at work, school, or in relationships?

Yes, it has completely ruined my daily life. I went from never missing a shift or class to calling out of work, skipping my GED tests, and completely ignoring texts from my friends and church group. On the worst days, I can't even force myself to shower or cook, so my aunt has to bring me food.
